mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of lines are parallel?

options.A: Two lines that cross at a point
options.B: Two lines that never meet and are the same distance apart
options.C: Two lines that form a right angle

mcqs.answer: Two lines that never meet and are the same distance apart
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are defined as lines in the same plane that never intersect and stay the same distance apart. Option B matches this definition. Options A, C, and D describe intersecting or perpendicular lines, not parallel lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that parallel lines remain equally separated
mcqs.question: What is true about the distance between two parallel lines?

options.A: The distance varies at different points
options.B: The distance is zero because they touch each other

mcqs.explanation: A key property of parallel lines is that the perpendicular distance between them is constant throughout their length. Hence option C is correct. Option A contradicts the definition, B is false because they never meet, and D is a misconception not applicable to Euclidean geometry.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in geometric figures
mcqs.question: Which of the following geometric figures contains a pair of parallel sides?
mcqs.explanation: In a rectangle, opposite sides are parallel and equal in length, satisfying the definition of parallel lines. A triangle has no parallel sides, an irregular quadrilateral may have none, and a circle has no straight sides.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify examples of parallel lines in everyday objects
mcqs.question: Which everyday object best illustrates parallel lines?
mcqs.explanation: Railway tracks consist of two long metal rails that run side by side without meeting, staying the same distance apart—an everyday example of parallel lines. The other options do not contain straight, non‑intersecting, equally spaced lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish parallel lines from intersecting lines
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes parallel lines from intersecting lines?

options.A: Parallel lines intersect at right angles
options.C: Parallel lines never meet, while intersecting lines meet at a point
options.D: Parallel and intersecting lines are the same

mcqs.answer: Parallel lines never meet, while intersecting lines meet at a point
mcqs.explanation: By definition, parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never cross; intersecting lines cross each other at a single point. Option C captures this distinction. Options A, B, and D are incorrect definitions.

mcqs.question: In a garden, two rows of plants are planted so that, no matter how far they are extended, the rows never meet. What type of lines do these rows represent?
mcqs.explanation: The description matches parallel lines: they lie in the same plane, never intersect, and stay equally spaced. Intersecting lines would meet, curved lines are not straight, and perpendicular lines intersect at a right angle.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that parallel lines remain equally separated
mcqs.question: A student claims that parallel lines get closer together as they extend farther apart. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The lines indeed get closer together
options.B: The lines stay equally spaced at all points
options.C: The lines will eventually cross each other
options.D: The lines diverge and become farther apart

mcqs.answer: The lines stay equally spaced at all points
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines maintain a constant perpendicular distance; they neither converge nor diverge. Therefore option B is correct. Options A, C, and D reflect common misconceptions about parallelism.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in geometric figures
mcqs.question: In a diagram, a transversal cuts two lines AB and CD and creates a pair of equal interior angles on the same side of the transversal. What can be concluded about AB and CD?
mcqs.explanation: If a transversal creates equal interior angles on the same side, the two lines are parallel (converse of the Alternate Interior Angles Theorem). Hence AB and CD are parallel. The other options do not follow from the given angle relationship.
